date: 2026-07-07 (threshold); 2026-07-08 (divergence)
documentation_shape: Program application fee US$150, applicant fee US$1,000 (US$750/dependent), the program's own ID card (QRP card) US$200/card, annual renewal US$25; a Ministry of National Security security-clearance check; and — per the program's own qualifying-income list (Pension, Annuity, Social Security Benefits, Investment Account, Inheritance, Reverse Mortgage, Personal Savings, Retirement Contribution Plans, and other means of retirement income) — proof the qualifying $2,000/month is drawn from one of these named sources. A real, documented practical hurdle beyond the paper checklist: at least one applicant account describes the $2,000/month needing to be shown as 'forwarded to a reputable financial institution within Belize,' which creates a catch-22 for applicants who can't open a Belizean bank account until residency status is further along — resolved in that one case only by appealing directly to the Central Bank via a correspondent bank.

documentation_shape: Required documentation per thehorizonrealestate.com's own "Requirements for Obtaining Real Estate Residency" list: "A registered title deed or notarized sales contract"; "A certificate from the Real Estate Registry confirming ownership"; proof of bank transfer from abroad through an authorized Egyptian bank; passport copies of buyer and family members; personal photos per applicant; proof of residence in Egypt; a bank certificate confirming payment in foreign currency. This language reads as though it assumes freehold title — a real, load-bearing wrinkle for Dahab specifically, where usufruct rights are the only property instrument a foreigner can actually hold, since it's genuinely unconfirmed whether a usufruct document would satisfy this program's stated documentation standard or whether freehold is a hard requirement. This is the single most important open question about this route for a Dahab-based applicant: it determines whether the route is available there at all, or whether Dahab remains tourist-visa-only regardless of what's purchased.

unit: USD, lump-sum registered-investment capital, roughly (VND 3,000,000,000 — the ĐT3-tier floor — converted at ~26,200 VND/USD, 2026-08-09)
documentation_shape: ĐT1 ≥VND100bn (~$3.8M): visa up to 5yr, Temporary Residence Card (TRC) up to 10yr. ĐT2 VND50-<100bn (~$1.9-3.8M): visa up to 5yr, TRC up to 5yr (one source: 10yr). ĐT3 VND3-<50bn (~$114.5k-1.9M): visa up to 3yr, TRC up to 2-3yr (one source: 10yr — sources disagree on ĐT3's TRC ceiling specifically). ĐT4 <VND3bn (~<$114.5k): visa only, up to 12 months, no TRC.

converts_to_pr: Yes (conditional on the ZAR 37,000/month income being guaranteed for the applicant's lifetime — a lifelong state pension or irrevocable annuity specifically, per Immigration Act Section 27(e); an ordinary non-lifelong passive-income proof doesn't clear this specific gate even if it clears the visa's own income test)
accepts_passive_income: Yes (rental income, dividends, and interest from investments are all explicitly confirmed acceptable, combinable with each other and with pension payments — not limited to a formal pension/annuity instrument)
